mainTopic: Which foods and amounts are valid for an עירוב: beets, apples, wine, vinegar, and onions.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of raw beets. In one version, raw beets are valid for an עירוב and only half-cooked beets are dangerous. In another version, רב המנונא forbids raw beets because רב חסדא said they kill. רב חסדא then praises well-cooked beets, and אביי adds that they must be fully boiled. Next, רבא invites questions like בן עזאי, and a scholar asks how many apples an עירוב needs. The גמרא proves from the משנה of כל האוכלין מצטרפין that apples are valid, and רב נחמן rules that a קב is needed. A challenge from a ברייתא that lists five peaches is answered, and רב יוסף shows that רב's 'and the same for עירוב' belongs to the משנה about gifts to the poor. This is confirmed by רב's rule of two רביעיות of wine. The גמרא then discusses combining foods, cooked wine, vinegar, and onions: onion bulbs are valid, but harmful onion leaves are not. The amud ends in the middle of a further limit on the danger of onion leaves, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The deadly beet is a half-cooked one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier challenge from רב חסדא's statement. The beet that 'kills' is one that is only partly cooked.
steps.simpleTranslation: That statement is talking about a beet that is cooked but not fully cooked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a challenge on the previous amud. רב המנונא allowed an עירוב with raw beets, but רב חסדא said raw beets kill, so the גמרא explains that רב חסדא meant half-cooked beets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There seemed to be a conflict between 'raw beets are fine for an עירוב' and 'raw beets kill.' The answer narrows רב חסדא's warning: the danger is a beet that is partly cooked, not a fully raw one. So raw beets stay usable as food for an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: That one, meaning that statement or case
Cooked and not cooked, meaning half-cooked

phrases.english: That is referring to one that is cooked and not cooked (half-cooked).
phrases.notes: Answers a קשיא from the previous part of the daf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge earlier against רב המנונא's ruling that raw beets are valid.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the deadly beet is a half-cooked one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא's 'raw beet kills' seemed to mean fully raw beets, which would make them unfit as food for an עירוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only half-cooked beets are dangerous, so raw beets remain acceptable.

steps.title: Second version: רב המנונא forbids raw beets
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב המנונא rules that raw beets may NOT be used for an עירוב. His reason is רב חסדא's statement that raw beets kill a healthy person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רב המנונא said: One may not make an עירוב with raw beets, because רב חסדא said: a raw beet kills a healthy man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, opposite version of רב המנונא's ruling. In this version he says raw beets cannot be used for an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב חסדא's statement was a challenge against רב המנונא. Here it becomes the reason for his ruling. Food that is dangerous to eat does not count as food for an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say, introducing another version of the tradition
We make an עירוב
Beets
Beet, in Aramaic
A healthy (literally 'living') man

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful: the word חַיָּיא appears twice. With סילקא it means 'raw,' and with גברא it means 'healthy.' The pun is part of the saying.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rav Hamnuna said:
One may not make an eiruv with raw beets,
as Rav Chisda said:
A raw beet kills a healthy man.
phrases.notes: There's a play on words here: חייא means both 'raw' and 'alive.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an alternate tradition in which רב חסדא's statement supports רב המנונא instead of challenging him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Raw beets may not be used for an עירוב, because they are dangerous to eat.

steps.title: But people eat raw beets and live
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's claim from what we see every day: people eat raw beets and do not die.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we see that people eat them and do not die!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that raw beets kill. It points to real life, where people eat them safely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a challenge from observation, not from a text. If raw beets were deadly, we would see people die from them. Since we don't, רב חסדא's statement needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: But we see, introducing a challenge from observation
They die

phrases.english: But don't we see
that people eat it and do not die?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָא חָזֵינַן דְּקָא אָכְלִי וְלָא מָיְיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the factual basis (רב חסדא's warning) of the second version.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's statement that a raw beet kills a healthy man.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everyday experience shows people eat raw beets without dying, which contradicts the claim.

steps.title: Again: the danger is a half-cooked beet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with the same words, הָתָם בִּבְשִׁיל וְלָא בְּשִׁיל. In this version, the beets people eat and survive are the partly cooked ones, while fully raw beets really are deadly.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about a beet that is cooked but not fully cooked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The people we see eating beets and living are eating partly cooked ones, not fully raw ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the answer must support רב המנונא's ruling, which forbids raw beets. So the beets we see people eat safely are ones that are partly cooked. A fully raw beet is still deadly, as רב חסדא said, and that is why it cannot be used for an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that statement

steps.whatToRemember: The two versions use the same words, בשיל ולא בשיל, in opposite ways. In the first, only a half-cooked beet is dangerous, so raw beets are valid for an עירוב. In the second, the half-cooked beets are the safe ones people eat, while raw beets kill and are invalid for an עירוב.

phrases.english: There, it refers to one that is cooked and not cooked (half-cooked).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from observation by explaining that the beets people eat safely are partly cooked, so רב חסדא's warning about raw beets stands.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The warning seemed to apply to every raw beet, which conflicts with what we see.
steps.terutzMaskana: People who eat beets and survive are eating partly cooked ones. Fully raw beets remain deadly, so they are invalid for an עירוב.

steps.title: Cooked beets are healthy
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא praises a cooked dish of beets: it is good for the heart and the eyes, and even more so for the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: A cooked dish of beets is good for the heart and good for the eyes, and all the more so for the intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another statement from רב חסדא about beets. This time it is about the health benefits of cooked beets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having discussed raw and half-cooked beets, the גמרא now gives the positive side: properly cooked beets are healthy. 'כל שכן' means they help the digestive system even more than the heart and eyes.

keyTerms.meaning: A cooked dish
All the more so
The intestines

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A cooked dish of beets
is beneficial for the heart and good for the eyes,
and all the more so for the intestines.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: תַּבְשִׁיל שֶׁל תְּרָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the beet theme with a related statement about the benefits of cooked beets.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cooked beets are healthy for the heart and eyes, and especially for the intestines.

steps.title: אביי: only when fully boiled
steps.stepSummary: אביי qualifies רב חסדא's praise. The beets are healthy only when they sit on the stove and boil until they bubble ('tukh tukh').
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: That is only when it sits on the stove and goes 'tukh tukh' (boils well).
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a condition to רב חסדא's statement. The beets must be cooked very thoroughly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the earlier point: a half-cooked beet is harmful. The benefit comes only from beets that are fully boiled, shown by the bubbling sound.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is only when, introducing a condition
Stove
The bubbling sound of boiling

phrases.english: Abaye said:
That is when it sits on the stove
and makes a 'tukh tukh' (boiling) sound.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וְהוּא דְּיָתֵיב אַבֵּי תָפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב חסדא's praise to beets that are thoroughly boiled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Beets are beneficial only when cooked until they boil thoroughly.

steps.title: רבא invites questions like בן עזאי
steps.stepSummary: רבא, in a happy and sharp mood, says he is like בן עזאי in the markets of טבריא, ready to answer any question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I am like בן עזאי in the markets of טבריא.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up a short story. רבא declares he can answer any question, and the next lines show someone testing him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי was famous for his sharpness. He would sit in the markets of טבריא and answer every question. רבא compares himself to him, which opens a question about using apples for an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Behold, I am
A תנא famous for his brilliance
The markets of טבריא

phrases.english: Rava said:
Behold, I am like ben Azzai
in the markets of Tiberias.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הֲרֵינִי כְּבֶן עַזַּאי בְּשׁוּקֵי טְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story that returns to the topic of which foods are used for an עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא announces he is ready to answer any question.

steps.title: How many apples for an עירוב?
steps.stepSummary: One of the scholars asks רבא how much apple is needed to make an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the scholars said to רבא: Apples, how many?
steps.whatsHappening: A scholar takes up רבא's invitation and asks a practical question. How many apples are needed for an עירוב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes apples are valid food for an עירוב and asks only about the amount. This assumption is exactly what רבא will challenge next.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the scholars
Apples
How much? (what amount)

phrases.english: One of the Sages said to Rava:
Apples, how many (are needed)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן לְרָבָא: תַּפּוּחִים בְּכַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבא's claim with a question about the amount of apples needed for an עירוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The required amount of apples for an עירוב.

steps.title: רבא asks back: can apples be used at all?
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers with a question of his own: is an עירוב even made with apples?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do we make an עירוב with apples?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not give an amount. Instead, he questions whether apples can be used for an עירוב at all, and the story continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא rejects the question's starting assumption. If apples are not valid for an עירוב, there is no amount to ask about. The next lines of the גמרא will test whether רבא's response is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it so that…? (a doubting, rhetorical question)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a reply in the form of a question. רבא is not asking for information; he is challenging the assumption that apples work for an עירוב.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Does one make an eiruv with apples?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the scholar by rejecting the assumption behind his question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא implies apples cannot be used for an עירוב, so the question of amount does not arise.

steps.title: A משנה seems to prove apples can be used for an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The scholar pushes back on רבא: a משנה says all foods combine for an עירוב, so apples should count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And apples can't be used? But we learned in a משנה: all foods combine to disqualify the body with half of a half-loaf, to reach the amount of two meals for an עירוב, and to reach an egg-bulk so they can become impure with food impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: The scholar challenges רבא's doubt that an עירוב can be made with apples. He quotes a משנה that lists three things all foods can combine for, one of which is an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had hinted that apples are not valid for an עירוב. The משנה says 'all foods' combine to reach the two-meal amount for an עירוב. Apples are food, so it seems they should qualify.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה? (opens a challenge from a משנה)
combine (different foods add up together to reach a required amount)
half of a half-loaf; eating this much impure food disqualifies the body
food for two meals, the required amount for an עירוב
an egg-bulk; the minimum size for food to transmit food impurity
the ritual impurity that applies to foods

phrases.english: And not?
phrases.notes: Can apples really not be used for an עירוב?

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: all foods combine
phrases.notes: Quoting a משנה

phrases.english: to disqualify the body with half of a half-loaf,
phrases.notes: Eating this amount of impure food disqualifies a כהן from eating תרומה

phrases.english: and for the food of two meals for an eruv,
and for an egg-bulk to become impure with food impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in Step 9 that an עירוב may not be made with apples.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's suggestion that apples are not valid for an עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says all foods combine for the two-meal amount of an עירוב; apples are food, so they should be valid.

steps.title: What exactly is the proof from the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what part of the משנה actually refutes רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the refutation here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask exactly how the משנה proves that apples work. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא tests two possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Quoting a משנה is not enough; the גמרא wants to locate the precise words that include apples. The steps that follow reject one reading and accept another.

keyTerms.meaning: a refutation; a strong challenge that disproves a position
what?

phrases.english: And what is this refutation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines how the challenge in Step 10 works.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words in the משנה actually show that apples are valid for an עירוב?

steps.title: The word 'all' alone cannot prove it
steps.stepSummary: If the proof is from 'all foods,' it fails, because רבי יוחנן teaches that we cannot learn from general rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the proof is because it taught 'all foods,' and apples are edible, didn't רבי יוחנן say: we do not learn from general rules, even where the rule says 'except'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first way to read the proof, from the word 'all,' and rejects it. רבי יוחנן's principle says general 'all' statements cannot be relied on to include every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Apples are edible, so they might seem to fall under 'all foods.' But רבי יוחנן teaches that general rules always have unstated exceptions, even when the rule already lists an exception with 'except.' So the word 'all' cannot prove that apples are included.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say; introduces a suggestion that will be rejected
fit for eating, edible
we do not learn from general rules
except; a word that lists an exception

steps.confusionAlert: Even a rule that already lists one exception with 'חוץ' is not complete. There can still be other exceptions it did not mention, so 'all' never guarantees full coverage.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוחנן's principle, אין למדין מן הכללות, appears throughout שס. It warns against treating words like 'כל' in a משנה as an airtight, complete list.

phrases.english: If you say it is because it taught 'all foods,'
and these apples are fit for eating,
but didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
we do not learn from general rules
even in a place where 'except' is stated!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects the first possible answer to the question in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only one reading of the proof, the one based on the word 'all.' The challenge itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: General 'all' statements always have exceptions, as רבי יוחנן teaches, so they cannot prove that a specific item is included.

steps.title: The real proof: the link between עירוב and food impurity
steps.stepSummary: The proof comes from the משנה pairing the עירוב amount with the egg-bulk for food impurity. Apples can become impure as food, so they count for an עירוב too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof is because it taught 'for the food of two meals for an עירוב, and for an egg-bulk to become impure with food impurity.' And apples certainly can become impure with food impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true basis of the proof. The משנה puts the same group of foods in both rules, and apples clearly belong to the food-impurity group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses one list of foods for both עירוב and טומאת אוכלין. It is certain that apples can become impure as food, so they are part of that list. Since it is the same list, apples also combine for an עירוב, and the challenge to רבא is a real one.

keyTerms.meaning: rather; introduces the accepted explanation
able to become impure
also

steps.whatToRemember: The proof is not from the general word 'all.' It comes from the משנה tying עירוב to טומאת אוכלין. Apples can become impure as food, so they are valid for an עירוב.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because it taught
'and for the food of two meals for an eruv'
'and for an egg-bulk to become impure with food impurity.'

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי נָמֵי בְּנֵי טַמּוֹיֵי טוּמְאַת אוֹכָלִין נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: And these apples are also able to become impure with food impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading from Step 12 with the correct basis for the proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words in the משנה include apples?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The pairing of עירוב with טומאת אוכלין. Apples can become impure as food, so they belong to the list and are valid for an עירוב.

steps.title: Back to the question: how many apples?
steps.stepSummary: Now that apples are valid for an עירוב, the גמרא returns to the original question of the amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is needed?
steps.whatsHappening: Having shown that apples can be used, the גמרא goes back to the scholar's original question from Step 8. This short question sets up רב נחמן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detour about whether apples work at all is now settled. The original question about the required amount can finally be answered.

keyTerms.meaning: how much? how many?

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the question from Step 8 now that Step 13 established apples are valid.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What quantity of apples is needed for an עירוב?

steps.title: רב נחמן: a קב of apples
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the amount of apples needed for an עירוב is a קב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: apples, a קב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question: an עירוב made with apples needs a קב of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an עירוב needs enough food for two meals. A קב is a fairly large amount, which suggests that apples are measured generously because they are not very filling.

keyTerms.meaning: apples
a קב, a measure of volume (about 24 egg-bulks)

steps.whatToRemember: Apples are valid for an עירוב, and according to רב נחמן the required amount is a קב.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Apples: a kav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The required amount of apples for an עירוב is a קב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב made of apples requires a קב.

steps.title: Challenge from the list of minimum gifts to the poor
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gives small minimum amounts for gifts to a poor person, including five peaches. רב said the same amounts apply to עירוב. So why should apples need a full קב instead of five, like peaches?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: an עוכלא of spices, a ליטרא of vegetables, ten nuts, five peaches, two pomegranates, and one citron. And גורסק בר דרי said in the name of רב מנשיא בר שגובלי, in the name of רב: 'And the same is true for עירוב.' So apples should also be like peaches!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן's ruling that apples for an עירוב must measure a קב. It cites a source suggesting that a small number of fruits is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the smallest amounts you may give a poor person, such as five peaches. רב supposedly said these same amounts are enough for an עירוב. Apples are about the size of peaches, so five apples should be enough, not a whole קב.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא or משנה)
A small measure, one eighth of a לוג
Peaches
A ליטרא, a unit of weight
And the same is true for an עירוב

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
An ukla of spices, and a liter of vegetables,
phrases.notes: These are the minimum amounts given to a poor person.

phrases.english: and ten nuts, and five peaches,
and two pomegranates, and one citron.
And Gursak bar Darei said
in the name of Rav Menashya bar Sheguvlei
in the name of Rav: And the same is true for an eiruv.
So these (apples) should also be like peaches!
phrases.notes: If five peaches are enough, five apples should be enough too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling that apples for an עירוב require a קב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that a קב of apples is needed for an עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב, the ברייתא's small amounts (five peaches) also apply to עירוב. Apples are similar to peaches, so a few apples should be enough.

steps.title: Peaches are important, apples are not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that peaches are a prized fruit, so even five of them count. Apples are ordinary, so a larger amount is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: These (peaches) are important, and these (apples) are not important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן by showing that peaches and apples are not really comparable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Five peaches can stand in for a meal-worthy amount because peaches are valued. Apples are not valued the same way, so five apples would not be significant. That is why apples still need a קב.

keyTerms.meaning: They are important / valued
They are not important

phrases.english: These are important, and these are not important.
phrases.notes: Peaches are important; apples are not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by distinguishing peaches from apples.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Apples are similar to peaches, so five should be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Peaches are prized, so a small number counts. Apples are not, so a קב is needed.

steps.title: רב יוסף says רב's statement was attached to the wrong source
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says רב מנשיא בר שגובלי made a mistake. רב יוסף had told him רב's statement 'and the same for עירוב' about a משנה, but רב מנשיא repeated it about the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: May his Master (God) forgive רב מנשיא בר שגובלי! I told it to him about a משנה, and he said it about the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף corrects the record. רב's comment 'and the same for עירוב' belongs to a משנה, not to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the basis of the challenge in step 16 at its root. If רב never linked עירוב to the ברייתא's list, then its 'five peaches' says nothing about עירוב amounts. The next step quotes the משנה רב was really talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: May his Master forgive him (said about someone who made a mistake)
About a משנה
About a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not disagreeing with רב. He is saying that רב's words were applied to the wrong source.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁרָא לֵיהּ מָרֵיהּ לְרַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר שְׂגוּבְלִי,
phrases.english: May his Master forgive Rav Menashya bar Sheguvlei,
I said it to him about a mishna,
and he said it about the baraita.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: שְׁרָא לֵיהּ מָרֵיהּ לְרַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר שְׂגוּבְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Instead of relying on the distinction in step 17, it removes the source of the challenge by correcting where רב's statement belongs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's statement 'and the same for עירוב' was said about a משנה, not about רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ברייתא.

steps.title: The משנה רב was really talking about
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes the משנה about the minimum gift to a poor person at the threshing floor. Its final rule, from אבא שאול, is that other fruits must be enough to sell and buy food for two meals. רב said about this משנה: 'and the same for עירוב.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: We may not give a poor person at the threshing floor less than half a קב of wheat or a קב of barley. רבי מאיר says: half a קב of barley. And a קב and a half of spelt, and a קב of dried figs or a מנה of pressed figs. רבי עקיבא says: half a מנה. And half a לוג of wine. רבי עקיבא says: a רביעית. And a רביעית of oil. רבי עקיבא says: an eighth. And for all other fruits, אבא שאול said: enough that he can sell them and buy food for two meals with them. And רב said: the same is true for עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף backs up his correction by quoting the משנה that רב's statement actually belongs to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה measures the gift by food value, ending with 'enough to buy two meals.' That matches the basic עירוב measure of food for two meals. So it makes sense that רב compared עירוב to this משנה and not to the ברייתא's short list of small fruit counts.

keyTerms.meaning: At the threshing floor, where מעשר עני is handed out
Spelt
Dried figs
A cake of pressed figs
Half (here, half a מנה)
Food for two meals

steps.whyThisMatters: It moves the source for עירוב amounts away from a list that included 'five peaches' to a משנה built on a food-value standard.

phrases.english: As we learned: We do not give less to a poor person at the threshing floor
than half a kav of wheat and a kav of barley.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: חֲצִי קַב שְׂעוֹרִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: half a kav of barley.
And a kav and a half of spelt,
and a kav of dried figs or a maneh of pressed figs.
Rabbi Akiva says: half (a maneh).

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲצִי לוֹג יַיִן, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: רְבִיעִית.
phrases.english: And half a log of wine; Rabbi Akiva says: a quarter (log).

phrases.aramaic: וּרְבִיעִית שֶׁמֶן, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: שְׁמִינִית.
phrases.english: And a quarter (log) of oil; Rabbi Akiva says: an eighth.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁאָר כׇּל הַפֵּירוֹת, אָמַר אַבָּא שָׁאוּל:
phrases.english: And for all other fruits, Abba Shaul said:
enough that he can sell them and buy with them
food for two meals.
And Rav said: And the same is true for an eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the משנה that רב יוסף says רב was really talking about.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that רב's statement belongs to the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about gifts to the poor at the threshing floor, followed by רב's comment 'and the same for עירוב.'

steps.title: Why is the משנה a better fit than the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes the משנה more suitable than the ברייתא for רב's comment about עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what makes this one stronger than that one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב יוסף's sharp reaction. Both sources deal with gifts to the poor, so why must רב's comment belong to one and not the other? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both the משנה and the ברייתא list minimum gifts to a poor person, it is not obvious why רב's comment could only fit the משנה. The גמרא wants the reason the ברייתא is unsuitable for עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: What is its strength / advantage?
Of this one over that one

phrases.english: And what is the strength of this one over that one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רב יוסף's claim that רב's statement could only have been about the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב's comment about עירוב fits the משנה better than the ברייתא.

steps.title: Spices are not the reason, since wheat and barley are not ready to eat either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא is unsuitable because it lists spices, which are not eaten on their own. It rejects this, because the משנה lists wheat and barley, which also are not ready to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because that one (the ברייתא) teaches spices, and spices are not things you eat, is it not true that here (the משנה) teaches wheat and barley, and they too are not things you eat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes one answer to its own question and immediately knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suggested reason: an עירוב must be real food, and spices are not eaten alone, so the ברייתא could not be about עירוב. The flaw: raw wheat and barley must be ground and cooked before eating, yet they appear in the משנה. So 'not edible as is' cannot be what separates the two sources.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
Spices
Fit to be eaten as they are
Is it really so that...? (introduces a rhetorical rejection)

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא תָּנֵי בְּהָךְ תַּבְלִין,
phrases.english: If you say it is because that one teaches spices,
and spices are not things fit for eating —

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ הָכָא מִי לָא קָתָנֵי חִטִּין וּשְׂעוֹרִין,
phrases.english: but does it not teach wheat and barley here,
and they are not fit for eating (as they are)!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא תָּנֵי בְּהָךְ תַּבְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes and rejects one possible answer to the question in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the ברייתא was unsuitable for עירוב because it includes spices.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה also includes items that are not ready to eat (raw wheat and barley), so this cannot be what makes the משנה better.

steps.title: The wine amount shows רב was speaking about the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה requires half a לוג of wine, and רב rules that an עירוב of wine needs two רביעיות, which equals half a לוג. Since the amounts match, רב's comment 'and the same for עירוב' must have been said about the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason is that the משנה says half a לוג of wine. And רב said: one may make an עירוב with two רביעיות of wine. Since we need that much, learn from this that when רב said 'and the same for עירוב,' he said it about this משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: After the spice idea was rejected in Step 21, the גמרא gives the real reason the משנה fits רב's comment better than the ברייתא: the wine amounts match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires half a לוג of wine for a poor person. רב has a separate rule that an עירוב of wine needs two רביעיות, which is exactly half a לוג. Because the משנה's wine amount matches רב's own עירוב amount, we know his comment 'and the same for עירוב' was attached to the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a לוג, a liquid measure
Two quarters of a לוג, which together equal half a לוג
One may make an עירוב
This much, so large an amount

steps.confusionAlert: Two רביעיות is not a new amount. It equals exactly half a לוג. That is why it matches the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָתָנֵי חֲצִי לוֹג יַיִן,
phrases.english: Rather, it is because it teaches half a log of wine,
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה about gifts to the poor.

phrases.english: and Rav said:
One may make an eruv with two quarters of wine.
phrases.notes: Two quarters of a לוג equal half a לוג.

phrases.english: Since we require this much,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כִּי אָמַר רַב ״וְכֵן לְעֵירוּב״ —
phrases.english: learn from it that when Rav said 'and the same for eruv,'
he said it about this Mishnah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָתָנֵי חֲצִי לוֹג יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected spice explanation from Step 21 with the correct reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Matching amounts: the משנה's wine amount matches רב's own עירוב amount
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The spices in the ברייתא might have made it unsuitable for עירוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's half לוג of wine matches רב's rule of two רביעיות for an עירוב, so his comment belongs to the משנה.

steps.title: Conclusion: רב's comment belongs to the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא confirms the point: learn from this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion and accepts that רב's comment was about the משנה, as רב יוסף said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms רב יוסף's claim from Step 18 that רב מנשיא בר שגובלי attached רב's comment to the wrong source. The משנה, not the ברייתא, is the source for the עירוב amounts.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this. A formula accepting a conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: רב's 'and the same for עירוב' refers to the משנה about gifts to the poor. The proof is that its half לוג of wine matches רב's own rule of two רביעיות of wine for an עירוב.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the reasoning of Step 22 as final.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב's comment about עירוב was said about the משנה, confirming רב יוסף.

steps.title: רב יוסף thinks each meal must be one kind of food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line 'food for two meals for עירוב.' רב יוסף thinks this means you need one full meal of one food and one full meal of another food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'and food for two meals for עירוב.' רב יוסף wanted to say: only if there is a meal from this food and a meal from that food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the earlier teaching and presents רב יוסף's understanding of it. This sets up רבה's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching says different foods combine to make up two meals for an עירוב. רב יוסף reads this narrowly: each meal must be complete from a single food. In his view, foods can be combined only as whole meals.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said. Introduces a quote from a teaching just cited
Food for two meals, the standard amount for an עירוב
He thought to say. Introduces an idea that will be rejected

steps.confusionAlert: 'סבר רב יוסף למימר' tells you this is only a first thought. It is rejected right away by רבה.

phrases.english: The Master said:
And with food for two meals for eruv.
phrases.notes: Different foods combine to make up this amount.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef thought to say:
only if there is a meal from this one
and a meal from that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: וּבִמְזוֹן שְׁתֵּי סְעוּדוֹת לְעֵירוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה of כל האוכלין מצטרפין quoted in step 10 and examines its clause about combining foods for two meals of an עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף: foods combine for an עירוב only when each meal is made entirely of one food.

steps.title: רבה: foods combine in any proportion
steps.stepSummary: רבה tells רב יוסף that the foods combine even if each one makes up only half, a third, or a quarter of a meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: even half, a third, or a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה rejects רב יוסף's narrow reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבה, there is no need for a full meal of each food. Any mix of foods that adds up to two meals is valid for an עירוב, even small fractions of each.

keyTerms.meaning: For a half, a third, or a quarter, meaning in any proportion

steps.whatToRemember: For an עירוב, different foods can be mixed in any proportion, as long as together they make two meals.

phrases.english: Rabba said to him:
Even for a half, a third, or a quarter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה: אֲפִילּוּ לְמֶחֱצָה לִשְׁלִישׁ וְלִרְבִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's reading from Step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב יוסף's requirement of one full meal from each food.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule of combining foods does not require whole meals. Any fraction of each food counts.

steps.title: Returning to רב's rule about wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now examines רב's statement itself: an עירוב of wine needs two רביעיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רב said: one may make an עירוב with two רביעיות of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב's wine rule, which was quoted earlier only as a proof, to look at it on its own. This sets up a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, רב's rule was used only to prove which source his comment belonged to. Now the גמרא asks whether the rule itself is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. The גמרא returns to examine a statement quoted earlier in passing

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav said:
One may make an eruv with two quarters of wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the statement used as evidence in Step 22 and makes it the topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב of wine requires two רביעיות, which is half a לוג.

steps.title: A ברייתא suggests much less wine is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether that much wine is really needed. A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says wine is measured only as enough to eat bread with it for two meals, which is far less.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really need that much? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: wine, enough to eat bread with it. Vinegar, enough to dip in it. Olives and onions, enough to eat with them. All of these are for two meals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's large wine amount from a ברייתא that sets a much smaller amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, wine counts as a side item: you only need enough to dip your bread in for two meals. That is a small amount, far less than half a לוג. So the ברייתא seems to contradict רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we really need? Introduces a challenge
But was it not taught in a ברייתא? Introduces a contradicting source
To dip food in
Vinegar

phrases.english: But do we need so much?
But was it not taught:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Wine, enough to eat with it,
phrases.notes: Enough to soak bread in so it can be eaten.

phrases.english: vinegar, enough to dip in it,
olives and onions, enough to eat with them
for two meals?
phrases.notes: This applies to all the items listed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule just restated in Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that an עירוב of wine needs two רביעיות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא measures wine only as a dip for bread over two meals, which is much less than half a לוג.

steps.title: The ברייתא speaks about cooked wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about cooked wine, which is strong, so a small amount is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about cooked wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying the two sources deal with different kinds of wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooked wine is very strong and is used only a little at a time as a dip, so a small amount covers two meals. רב is speaking about regular wine, which people drink, so half a לוג is needed. The two sources do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in the other source
Cooked wine, which is very strong

steps.whatToRemember: Regular wine for an עירוב: two רביעיות (half a לוג), as רב said. Cooked wine: only enough to dip bread in for two meals, as the ברייתא says.

phrases.english: There, it is about cooked wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases: the ברייתא is about cooked wine, רב is about regular wine
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to set a small amount for all wine, contradicting רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's small amount applies only to strong cooked wine. Regular wine needs half a לוג, as רב said.

steps.title: How much vinegar is needed for an eruv
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says vinegar for an עירוב must be enough to dip food in. רב גידל in the name of רב explains that this means enough to dip the food of two meals made up of vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: vinegar, enough to dip food in it. רב גידל said in the name of רב: enough to dip in it the food of two meals of vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next food on the ברייתא's list, vinegar. It explains what 'enough to dip' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar is not eaten alone. It is a dip, so it is measured by how much food it can serve. רב sets the standard as two full meals made only of vegetables. That needs a fairly large amount of vinegar, because a vegetable-only meal is a lot of vegetables.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said.' This formula re-quotes a line from a ברייתא already cited, so the גמרא can analyze it.
Vinegar
To dip food into something
Vegetables

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: חוֹמֶץ כְּדֵי לְטַבֵּל בּוֹ.
phrases.english: The Master said: vinegar, enough to dip in it.
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא again

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
enough to dip in it
the food of two meals made of vegetables.
phrases.notes: Meals made entirely of vegetables, which is a large quantity

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: חוֹמֶץ כְּדֵי לְטַבֵּל בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wine measurement (steps 26-28) to the next item in the same ברייתא, vinegar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vinegar for an עירוב must be enough to dip two meals' worth of vegetable-only food.

steps.title: A second version of רב's vinegar measurement
steps.stepSummary: Some report רב's words differently. In this version the vinegar only needs to be enough for the vegetables that are eaten during two ordinary meals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רב גידל said in the name of רב: enough for the vegetables that are eaten in two meals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of what רב said about the vinegar amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version the meals are made entirely of vegetables. In this version the meals are regular meals, and you only count the vegetables normally eaten alongside them. That is a much smaller amount of vegetables, so less vinegar is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Some say.' This introduces a different report of the same statement.
That is eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions come from the same people, רב גידל in the name of רב. This is not two אמוראים arguing. It is one statement remembered in two ways, and the second version gives a smaller amount.

phrases.english: Some say,
Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
enough for the vegetables that are eaten in two meals.
phrases.notes: Only the side vegetables of normal meals, which is less

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate, more lenient version of the measurement in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vinegar only needs to cover the vegetables normally eaten in two ordinary meals.

steps.title: How many olives and onions are needed for an eruv
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says olives and onions for an עירוב must be enough to eat with the food of two meals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: olives and onions, enough to eat with them the food of two meals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא, about olives and onions. This sets up a challenge about onions that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Olives and onions are side foods eaten with bread, so they are measured by how much you would eat alongside two meals. By putting onions on the list, the ברייתא implies that an עירוב of onions is valid. The next step questions exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: Olives
Onions

phrases.english: The Master said: olives and onions,
enough to eat with them
the food of two meals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Olives and onions count for an עירוב in the amount eaten alongside two meals.

steps.title: A story where רבי מאיר rejected an onion eruv
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether onions can really be used for an עירוב. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר tells of a man who made an עירוב of onions so he could walk to טיבעין. רבי מאיר told him he could not move beyond his four אמות, which shows the onion עירוב did not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can one really make an עירוב with onions? It was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said, Once רבי מאיר spent שבת in ערדיסקא. A man came before him and said, 'רבי, I made an עירוב with onions to go to טיבעין.' רבי מאיר made him stay within his four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's ruling that onions are valid for an עירוב. It brings a story that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the onion עירוב had worked, the man could have walked toward טיבעין. רבי מאיר confined him to four אמות, which means he treated the man as having left his תחום with no valid עירוב. So onions seem to be invalid, which contradicts the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Make an עירוב
'But it was taught.' This introduces a ברייתא that contradicts what was just said.
I made an עירוב
Four אמות, the small area a person may move in after going beyond the תחום

phrases.english: And with onions, may one make an eruv?
But it was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת שָׁבַת רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּעַרְדִּיסְקָא,
phrases.english: Once Rabbi Meir spent Shabbat in Ardiska,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא אָדָם אֶחָד לְפָנָיו, אָמַר לוֹ:
phrases.english: and a certain man came before him and said to him:
Rabbi, I made an eruv with onions to go to Tiv'in,
phrases.notes: An עירוב תחומין meant to let him walk to that town

phrases.aramaic: וְהוֹשִׁיבוֹ רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Meir made him stay within his four cubits.
phrases.notes: This means the onion עירוב was not valid

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the onion part of the ruling in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that onions may be used for an עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction between sources. רבי מאיר's ruling treats an onion עירוב as invalid.

steps.title: Onion leaves versus onion bulbs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two sources are talking about different parts of the onion. The story with רבי מאיר is about the leaves, which are invalid. The ברייתא is about the bulbs, which are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This source is about the leaves, and that source is about the bulbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the case into two parts of the onion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Onion leaves were considered harmful, so they are not proper food for an עירוב. That is why רבי מאיר rejected that man's עירוב. Onion bulbs are normal, healthy food, so the ברייתא's ruling holds for them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult.' This introduces an answer that shows two sources deal with different cases.
Leaves, here meaning the green onion leaves
Literally 'mothers,' meaning the onion bulbs

steps.whatToRemember: An עירוב needs real, healthy food. Onion bulbs qualify. Onion leaves, which were seen as harmful, do not.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about leaves, that one is about bulbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּעָלִים, הָא בְּאִימָּהוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different part of the onion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Onions are one food, so the two sources seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Leaves are invalid because they are harmful. Bulbs are valid.

steps.title: Proof that onion leaves are dangerous
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if someone ate an onion and died the next morning, we do not need to ask what killed him. שמואל says this danger applies only to the leaves, not to the bulbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If someone ate an onion, got up early, and died, we do not ask what he died from. And שמואל said: They only taught this about the leaves, but about the bulbs we have no concern.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer that onion leaves are harmful while bulbs are safe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats eating an onion as dangerous enough to explain a sudden death. שמואל limits that danger to the leaves. This backs up the split made in step 33, since harmful leaves cannot count as food for an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it was taught.' This introduces a ברייתא brought as support.
And he got up early, meaning by the next morning
'We have no concern with it.' There is no problem.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
If he ate an onion, got up early, and died,
we do not ask what he died from.
phrases.notes: The onion is assumed to be the cause

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בֶּעָלִים,
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: They only taught this about the leaves,
but about the bulbs, we have no concern.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the leaves-versus-bulbs answer given in step 33.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that onion leaves are harmful and onion bulbs are not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about death after eating an onion, as explained by שמואל.

steps.title: Starting to limit the danger of onion leaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to say that even the danger of onion leaves applies only in a certain situation. The sentence continues into the next passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even about the leaves, we only said this when...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a further limit on the warning about onion leaves. The details come in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 34 showed that only the leaves are dangerous. Now the גמרא narrows the rule further: even the leaves are dangerous only under certain conditions, which are about to be spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: Also / even
'We only said this when.' This introduces a limit on a rule.

phrases.english: And even with leaves, we only said this when
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the danger of the leaves stated in step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the danger of onion leaves is limited to a specific situation, explained next.
